questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify and comment on the main themes peculiar to John's Gospel.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The Fourth Gospel differs from Matthew, Mark and Luke in structure, language and content. Its main themes are presented in the prologue and developed through the signs, discourses and the passion narrative. The author states his purpose in 20:30-31: that readers may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and have life in his name.

**1. The Word (Logos).** Jesus is the pre-existent Word who was with God, was God, and became flesh (1:1-18). This theme shows his divinity and his role in creation and revelation.

**2. Life and eternal life.** Life is offered to all who believe (3:16; 5:24; 10:10; 11:25).

**3. Light and darkness.** Jesus is the light of the world (1:4-9; 8:12; 9:5); people respond by coming to the light or preferring darkness (3:19-21).

**4. Truth.** Jesus is full of grace and truth (1:14) and says, "I am the way, and the truth, and the life" (14:6).

**5. Belief and unbelief.** The verb "to believe" is central. Signs lead to faith, but some refuse (12:37). Thomas' confession "My Lord and my God" is the climax (20:28).

**6. Signs and glory.** Seven signs reveal Jesus' glory: Cana, the official's son, the man at the pool, the feeding, the walking on the water, the blind man, and Lazarus (2:11; 4:46-54; 5; 6; 9; 11).

**7. The "I am" sayings.** Jesus describes himself as the bread of life, the light of the world, the gate, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, the truth and the life, and the true vine (6:35; 8:12; 10:7, 11; 11:25; 14:6; 15:1).

**8. Relationship of Father and Son.** Jesus does the works of the Father and is sent by him (5:19-30; 10:30; 14:9-11).

**9. The Holy Spirit as Paraclete.** The Spirit, the Advocate, will teach and remind the disciples after Jesus' departure (14:16-17, 26; 16:7-15).

**10. Love and unity.** The new commandment is to love one another (13:34-35), and Jesus prays that his followers may be one (17).

**11. The hour and glorification.** Jesus' death is his "hour", the moment when he is glorified (12:23; 13:1; 17:1).

**12. Replacement of Jewish institutions.** John shows Jesus fulfilling the Temple, feasts, purification and Sabbath (2:13-22; 4:21-24; 7:37-39).

**Comment.** The Gospel has no parables or exorcisms as the Synoptics do and speaks little of the kingdom of God; it stresses the identity of Jesus and the experience of eternal life now. Its themes are connected: the Word gives light and life to all who believe.

**Conclusion.** These distinctive themes make the Fourth Gospel a deeply theological account, aimed at faith.
